ip_top_stories.title: Publishers Accuse OpenAI of Withholding Evidence in Copyright Lawsuits
ip_top_stories.summary: News outlets have filed court motions urging a judge to sanction OpenAI, accusing the company of hiding and withholding evidence in high-stakes AI copyright litigation. The publishers allege OpenAI has failed to produce key materials relevant to how its models were trained on copyrighted content. The case represents a significant moment in the ongoing legal battle between media organisations and AI developers.

ip_top_stories.title: Over 100 Authors Sue Anthropic for Pirating Books to Train AI
ip_top_stories.summary: More than 100 authors have launched a lawsuit against Anthropic, alleging the AI company used pirated books without authorisation to train its AI models. The case adds to a growing wave of copyright litigation targeting major AI developers over their use of creative works in training datasets.

ip_top_stories.title: Midjourney Strikes Back: Sued AI Giant Demands Hollywood's Secrets
ip_top_stories.summary: Midjourney, which faces copyright litigation from artists, has gone on the offensive by demanding discovery of confidential information from Hollywood in its legal proceedings. The move signals an escalating and more combative phase in AI copyright disputes involving creative industries.

ip_top_stories.title: Press Groups Defend Copyright Proposal After Google Pushback
ip_top_stories.summary: Press and publishing groups have pushed back against Google's opposition to a copyright legislative proposal, with LBH Pers among those criticising the tech giant's stance. The dispute reflects ongoing tensions between news publishers and AI and technology companies over copyright protections for journalism.

ip_top_stories.title: Kenya Tribunal Rules AI Works Cannot Be Copyrighted
ip_top_stories.summary: A Kenyan tribunal has ruled that works generated by AI are not eligible for copyright protection, adding to an emerging body of international legal decisions on AI-generated content. The ruling comes as Kenyan creators are increasingly experimenting with AI tools to produce music and other content, while the copyright status of such works remains unresolved.

ip_further_links.title: Why AI Song Generators Don't Grant Copyright
ip_further_links.summary: An explainer examining why AI-generated music does not attract copyright protection, relevant to creators and platforms using generative audio tools.

ip_further_links.title: This Legal Battle Could Reshape AI
ip_further_links.summary: An analysis of how the current wave of AI copyright litigation could have far-reaching consequences for the development and regulation of AI systems.

ip_further_links.title: PM to Unveil AI Agenda as Government Seeks to Calm Copyright Concerns
ip_further_links.summary: The UK Prime Minister is set to announce a new AI policy agenda amid ongoing pressure from creators and publishers over copyright protections in relation to AI training.

ip_further_links.title: Kenyan Creators Betting on AI Models to Produce Hit Songs as Copyright Puzzle Lingers
ip_further_links.summary: Kenyan musicians are adopting AI tools to create commercial music while the legal framework around AI-generated content and copyright remains uncertain in the country.

ip_further_links.title: Artists Warned to 'Be Prepared to Make a Stand' Against AI
ip_further_links.summary: Creative industry figures are urging artists to take an active stance in defending their rights as AI companies continue to use creative works in training without clear licensing frameworks.

ip_further_links.title: Print Book Sales Flat in First Half of 2026 [Metered]
ip_further_links.summary: US print book sales showed no growth in the first half of 2026, according to new industry figures reported by Publishers Weekly.

ip_further_links.title: University of Chicago Press Workers Vote to Unionize [Metered]
ip_further_links.summary: Staff at University of Chicago Press have voted to form a union, in a development that reflects broader labour trends across academic publishing.

ip_further_links.title: Guest Post — Why Research Libraries Oppose the OMB Revisions to the Uniform Guidance
ip_further_links.summary: Research libraries set out their concerns about proposed US Office of Management and Budget changes to funding rules, arguing the revisions threaten open access and library operations.

ip_further_links.title: AI 'Distillation Attacks' Are Profoundly Stupid
ip_further_links.summary: A commentary piece argues that so-called AI distillation attacks — attempts to extract training data from AI models — are technically and legally misconceived.

ip_further_links.title: Computer Implemented Inventions at the UPC — Guidance for a Common Path
ip_further_links.summary: A guest post on IPKat examines the Unified Patent Court's emerging guidance on software and computer-implemented inventions, relevant to AI and IP practitioners in Europe.
